title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: dormancy period and dormant account fee by tier
content:
## Scope

This card gives, for each tier of Savings & Money Market Accounts, how long an account may go without customer-initiated activity before it becomes dormant, and the fee charged per statement cycle while it is dormant.

## Definitions

- **Dormancy period**: the number of calendar months without customer-initiated activity after which the account becomes dormant.
- **Dormant account fee**: the fee per statement cycle while the account is dormant, in USD; it never takes the balance below zero.

## Tier table

| Tier | Dormancy period | Dormant account fee per cycle |
|---|---|---|
| Starter Savings | 24 calendar months | USD 0.00 |
| Statement Savings | 24 calendar months | USD 3.00 |
| Goal Builder Savings | 24 calendar months | USD 0.00 |
| Money Market Account | 24 calendar months | USD 5.00 |
| Premier Money Market | 24 calendar months | USD 5.00 |
| Private Client Money Market | 36 calendar months | USD 0.00 |

## Points of judgement

**Which tier allows the longest inactivity before dormancy?** Private Client Money Market, at 36 calendar months; every other tier uses 24.

**Which tiers charge nothing while dormant?** Starter Savings, Goal Builder Savings and Private Client Money Market, each at USD 0.00.

**A dormant Statement Savings account holds USD 1.20 at cycle close. Can the dormant account fee take it below zero?** No; the fee never takes the balance below zero.
